title: Exact geometric stalks and the constant-complex retraction
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a commutative ring, and $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. On the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] let $A_T$ be the constant ring sheaf and $c(M)=\underline M$ the constant $A_T$-module sheaf of an ordinary $A$-module $M$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Write $S(F)=F_{\bar t}$ for the geometric stalk with its induced $A$-module action [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Use sheaves of modules over $A_T$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and apply $S$ and $c$ termwise to unbounded cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $C$ be any such complex of $A_T$-module sheaves and $E$ any such complex of ordinary $A$-modules. Both are exact additive functors on their respective abelian categories, and there are natural $A$-linear cohomology isomorphisms
$$H^n(SC)\cong S(H^n(C)),\qquad H^n(cE)\cong c(H^n(E))\quad(n\in\mathbf Z).$$
Consequently each termwise functor preserves acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms. There is a natural chain isomorphism $\eta_E:E\xrightarrow{\sim}S(cE)$ whose degree-$n$ component sends $e\in E^n$ to the germ at $(T,\bar t)$ of its constant section. In particular $S(A_T)\cong A$ has the ordinary scalar action. All assertions hold for arbitrary unbounded complexes, without any finiteness hypothesis on $A$.

proof.text: Use the already proved siteConstantModuleFunctorGeneral_exact, the exactness clause of [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor], for the recorded constant-module functor. It gives additivity and preservation of finite limits and colimits for arbitrary modules, with exactly the given sheafified-ring action.

By [lem-cbc-constant-ring-module-sheaves], the specified constantRingModuleRestriction is the forward functor of an additive equivalence. Compose it with the point sheaf fibre of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. The latter preserves finite limits by filtered-colimit exactness, as in [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], now applied directly in ModuleCat A; it preserves colimits by its skyscraper right adjoint. Restrict the known AB5 and filtered-colimit preservation instances from the coefficient universe to the point universe. Equivalences preserve limits and colimits, so the composite is exact and additive. No comparison of scalar actions is needed.

Whisker Mathlib ShortComplex.homologyFunctorIso for each exact functor by the short-complex functor in degree n, as in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. The result is definitionally the required natural cohomology isomorphism. ShortComplex.Exact.map gives preservation of acyclicity degree by degree, and HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_map_of_preservesHomology gives preservation of quasi-isomorphisms. There are no boundedness assumptions.

View the module-sheafification adjunction unit of [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] as a natural map from the constant fixed-ring module presheaf to the scalar restriction of c(M). Its components are exactly the underlying abelian sheafification unit. Local injectivity and surjectivity are therefore inherited from that unit. A point fibre sends any locally bijective map to a bijective module map. The fibre of the constant presheaf is M by [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram]. Compose the inverse of this constant-presheaf comparison with the fibre of the unit. The coprojection equation identifies its hom with the unit at the identity neighbourhood followed by the specified pointedEtaleGerm. Sheafification-unit naturality and fibre-coprojection naturality prove naturality in M. Apply the existing termwise NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex construction of [def-kun-constant-sheaf] to obtain the required natural chain isomorphism and its degreewise constant-germ formula.

For the regular module sheaf, the ring-sheafification unit defines a fixed-ring linear map from the constant presheaf A to the scalar restriction of A_T: its linearity is precisely multiplicativity of the ring unit. It is locally bijective on underlying sets. Apply the same constant-presheaf fibre construction and coprojection equation to obtain the normalized regular-module stalk isomorphism. The scalar action is exactly restriction along the ring unit, hence this is an isomorphism in ModuleCat A with its ordinary source action.
